Subject: Security exhibit + MSA redline questions — Valence Health

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal/procurement team reviewed the MSA and the security exhibit and attached a consolidated redline (Valence_SecExhibit_v3_redline.pdf). High-level asks from our side:

- Pen test window language: Valence needs a firm 30-day advance notice and a 14-day staging window where our team can validate scope.
- SOC 2: we ask for SOC 2 Type II report access for the most recent 12 months and an attestation that continuous monitoring is in place.
- Evidence cadence: we prefer quarterly evidence deliveries for selected artifacts (SOC, vulnerability scan summaries, key controls mapping) with a documented handoff owner.
- Audit rights: carveouts for production data inspection but allow for sampled/privileged inspection under NDA; we also want a draft checklist of what you’ll provide during an inspection.

Can your team confirm if the attached redline is acceptable in principle? If not, can you propose alternative language for pen-test scheduling and evidence cadence? We’re aiming to finalize before our procurement board on July 8.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Emily Park
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
Valence Health

Emily — thanks for the redline and clear asks. I’m including Laura (legal) and Karthik (assurance) to propose language and an operational plan. Quick responses below, more detailed follow-up by EOD tomorrow: 

- Pen test window: we typically require a 21-day notice for internal scheduling but can agree to 30 for enterprise customers. We need to preserve a short blackout carveout for emergency maintenance; we’ll propose exact wording.
- SOC 2: we can provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA and a lightweight controls map.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly cadence is reasonable; we’ll propose a template (owner, artifact, delivery mechanism).
- Audit rights: we prefer sampling + remote evidence first with an option for privileged onsite inspection under strict scoping.

Next steps: Laura will draft redline counter-proposal and we’ll include a proposed evidence cadence spreadsheet. Can you share the internal procurement timeline (you mentioned July 8)? We’ll aim to turn a counter by Friday 6/27.

— Irene

Emily — looping in formal redline text below and a short operational note. This is a mail-friendly summary; we’ll attach a PDF counter and a proposed-evidence-cadence.xlsx by EOD.

Draft counter-proposals (high level):
1) Pen Test Scheduling (new clause): "Customer shall provide Provider with not less than twenty-one (21) calendar days' notice prior to any penetration test that targets Provider-managed infrastructure. Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a staging window of up to fourteen (14) calendar days for Customer to validate scope and pre-test staging. Provider reserves the right to deny or limit any test that, in Provider's reasonable judgment, may materially impact other customers or platform stability; in such cases Provider will propose alternate timing."

2) SOC 2 Access (amendment): "Provider will provide Customer with a copy of the most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a consolidated Controls Mapping document within five (5) business days of execution of a mutual NDA. Provider maintains continuous monitoring and will provide evidence summaries at the cadence set forth in the Evidence Cadence Schedule."

3) Evidence Cadence (annex): quarterly delivery of selected artifacts (SOC report, vulnerability summary, control exception log, attestation of patching cadence). Each artifact will include an Owner (Redwood lead), Delivery Mechanism (secure share + encrypted link), and Turnaround SLAs for follow-up questions (10 business days).

4) Audit Rights (clarification): remote evidence review as the primary route; privileged onsite or interactive sessions require 30 days' mutual notice, narrowly scoped objectives, and an agreed list of sample artifacts. All on-site activities require a mutually executed inspection addendum and pre-approved access rules (including access window, endpoints, and data redaction responsibilities).

Operational note (Karthik): when we provide the quarterly bundle we will include a vulnerability heatmap (high/medium/low), a short executive summary, and an indexed evidence manifest — this should satisfy most procurement review boards. For pen tests we prefer an agreed scope limited to application and infra layers we own; third-party components (cloud provider managed services) will be handled via provider attestations, not direct scanning.

If Valence can accept these anchors, we’ll produce a marked PDF and the evidence cadence sheet for signature. If you need 30-day test notice in writing we can move 21 -> 30 with a reciprocal clause requiring Valence to provide a single test-window coordinator and to limit tests to non-production or agreed staging endpoints.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- For SOC 2: NDA is fine; can you confirm redactions allowed? We typically require a non-redacted report for legal review but understand sensitive provider details may be redacted — we’ll accept a small set of redactions if you list them.
- Evidence cadence sheet looks good; procurement will confirm owners.

If you can send the marked PDF and the evidence cadence spreadsheet we’ll aim to provide counter-sign feedback by Monday 6/30 so we stay on track for the July 8 procurement meeting.
